discovery: Development of high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy into a momentum-resolved probe of correlated electrons, revealing the d-wave superconducting gap and pseudogap in the cuprates

nominees.name: Zhi-Xun Shen
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Juan Carlos Campuzano
nominees.affiliation: University of Illinois Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (experimental; spectroscopy of quantum materials)
motivation: Shen and Campuzano turned angle-resolved photoemission from a band-mapping tool into a precision, momentum-resolved probe of many-body physics. Shen's 1993 measurement of a strongly anisotropic superconducting gap in Bi2212 gave the first direct momentum-space evidence for d-wave pairing in the cuprates, and both groups discovered and mapped the normal-state pseudogap, its Fermi arcs, and the anisotropic quasiparticle self-energy, including electron-boson coupling kinks. Their methodological advances, in energy and momentum resolution, lineshape analysis, and synchrotron and laser sources, established ARPES as the central experimental method for correlated electrons. The technique they built has since been decisive for topological insulators, iron-based superconductors, heavy-fermion and 2D materials, and now time-resolved studies of light-driven phases. Few experimental methods have so profoundly reshaped how physicists understand electrons in solids, and their foundational contributions have held up across materials, probes, and three decades of scrutiny.
